title: Assessment of motor development in newborns with congenital diaphragmatic hernia using motion sensors
summary:
This study investigates the motor development of children with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH), a rare defect of the diaphragm where abdominal organs may move into the chest. These children often require intensive medical care after birth and are at increased risk for developmental delays, especially in motor skills.
The aim of the study is to use small, CE-certified motion sensors to record the children’s natural movements in their home environment. The sensors are attached to the arms and legs, and the children play for at least one hour while their movements are measured. The data are then analyzed to identify potential developmental delays early and to compare them with normative values and standardized Bayley test results.
Participation is voluntary, non-invasive, and involves no additional risk. The results are intended to support early interventions and to improve understanding of the long-term motor development of children with CDH.

interventions.name: The study includes an observational group of infants and toddlers aged 8 to 24 months diagnosed with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) who were treated at the Neonatology Department of the University Hospital Bonn. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Diagnosed with congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH), treated at the Neonatology Department of the University Hospital Bonn.
- Written informed consent from parents or legal guardians.
- Parents/legal guardians must have sufficient German or English language skills to understand the study information and consent process.
Exclusion criteria:
- Absence of written informed consent from parents or legal guardians.
- Medical instability of the child that prevents safe participation in the assessments.
- Other medical or social conditions that would prevent safe completion of the motion sensor measurements.
